systems.name: The M-Lode: Complete Voice-Led Chord Family System
systems.summary: The M-Lode (Mother Lode) is the central system of both volumes combined: every 3-part and 4-part chord voicing within C Major, C Melodic Minor, and C Harmonic Minor, voice-led through all six diatonic cycles. Foundational principle: all of it is based on voice-leading. Traversal is governed by diatonic stepwise voice motion tracked through paired Intervallic and Functional Voice-Leading grids; common-tone preservation is a distinct analytical category. Modification rules: octave insertion, drop voicing derivation, single-voice omission to 3-part subsets, passing-tone filling of third-motion intervals.

traversal_rules.name: Diatonic Stepwise Voice Motion Through Six Cycles
traversal_rules.summary: Each voice moves by 2nd, 3rd, or common tone as the system traverses successive diatonic positions; tracked in Intervallic and Functional grids.

references.quote_excerpt: All of the M-Lode is based on voice-leading.

traversal_rules.name: Common-Tone Preservation Across Chord Positions
traversal_rules.summary: When a voice does not move between adjacent positions it is marked c.t. and is a distinct analytical category.

references.quote_excerpt: three voices sustain while one moves by a fourth

traversal_rules.name: Arpeggio Direction Alternation Across Successive Chords
traversal_rules.summary: When traversing positions through arpeggiation, ascend then descend on alternating chords.

references.quote_excerpt: Arpeggiate up the first chord, then down the second chord
arpeggiating up one chord and then down the next

traversal_rules.name: Drop-D Pedal String Traversal in D Dorian
traversal_rules.summary: Tune low E to D and use as pedal while cycling through 4th-voicing positions in D Dorian.

references.quote_excerpt: tune the low E string down a whole step to D. Use the low D string as a pedal
there aren’t any “avoid” notes in Dorian

traversal_rules.name: Cycles 2 and 7 Dual Voice-Leading Exception
traversal_rules.summary: Cycles 2 and 7 carry two voice-leadings each; diatonic 5th interval risks voice-crossing.

references.quote_excerpt: Cycles 2 and 7 have two different voice-leadings.
interval of a diatonic 5th that occurs in the movement from one inversion to the next

modification_rules.name: Octave Insertion Between Any Two Voices
modification_rules.summary: Any two voices may have an octave inserted between them.

references.quote_excerpt: inserting an octave between any 2 voices within a 3-part chord or a 4-part chord
Of course, all of this applies to the 3-part 4th voicings as well
do the “octave insertion thing” between the middle two voices

modification_rules.name: Single-Voice Omission to Derive 3-Part Subsets
modification_rules.summary: Drop any voice from a 4-part chord; 4 configurations.

references.quote_excerpt: it just amounts to leaving out one of the voices...] There are 4 possible configurations.
Play all 4 possible combinations of 3 voices

modification_rules.name: Passing-Tone Fill on Third-Motion Intervals
modification_rules.summary: When any voice moves by a 3rd, fill with a passing tone; scales across solo, counterpoint, 3-part, 4-part.

references.quote_excerpt: Anytime one of the voices moves a distance of a 3rd, you can fill in that interval with a melodic passing tone.
two voices move in 3rds

modification_rules.name: Drop Voicing Type Selection
modification_rules.summary: Close → Drop 2, Drop 3, Drop 4, Drop 2 & 3, Drop 2 & 4, Double Drop 2/Drop 4.

references.quote_excerpt: Drop 4 is an option.
only for finger-style guitarists] would be: Drop 3 and 4
Voicing Type: Drop 2

modification_rules.name: Quartal Voicing Interval Exclusion
modification_rules.summary: 3rds and 6ths are excluded as primary intervals in quartal context; diminished 4ths (B-Eb) sound triadic and must be avoided.

references.quote_excerpt: tertial harmony and quartal harmony are pretty much exact opposites.
they don’t work very well in a 4th voicings context.
Primary intervals: 4ths and 5ths

modification_rules.name: Density Floor: 4-Way Close as Minimum Starting Point
modification_rules.summary: Start practice with 4-way close voicings; seek open-string playable versions.

references.quote_excerpt: look at all of the 4-way close options within the M-Lode
find as many playable voicings for 4-way close as we can

systems.name: Exhaustive Voice-Combination Practice System
systems.summary: Practice every 2-voice and 3-voice subset of every 4-part chord. Joe's 2 Plus 2 Thing divides 4-voice chords into call-and-response 2-note pairs. Five deployment modes: melodies, arpeggios, counterpoint, 3-part chords, 4-part chords.

members.name: Full 4-Voice Chord Position
members.summary: Source from which subsets are derived.

traversal_rules.name: Exhaustive Combinatorial Traversal of Voice Subsets
traversal_rules.summary: Traverse all 6 two-voice subsets and all 4 three-voice subsets of every 4-part chord.

references.quote_excerpt: Play all 6 possible combinations of 2 voices
Play all 4 possible combinations of 3 voices
Play everything else in both books with the exception of 18 pages of triads and 30 pages of 3-part 4ths

traversal_rules.name: Joe's 2 Plus 2 Call-and-Response Alternation
traversal_rules.summary: 4-part chord → 2 alternating 2-note groupings as Q/A pairs.

references.quote_excerpt: divide the 4-part chord into two 2-note groupings
VERSION B shows a Joe's 2 Plus 2 Thing.
1. melodies 2. arpeggios 3. counterpoint (2 simultaneous voices) 4. 3-part chords 5. 4-part chords

modification_rules.name: 24-Sequence Arpeggio Permutation Rule
modification_rules.summary: Any 4-part voicing has 24 distinct arpeggio orderings.

references.quote_excerpt: Any [and ALL] 4-part voicings can be arpeggiated in 24 different sequences

modification_rules.name: C Harmonic Minor Scale Preference
modification_rules.summary: Prefer C Harmonic Minor for arpeggio/voicing exploration.

references.quote_excerpt: IT JUST SOUNDS BETTER IN HARMONIC MINOR
